title: Keep an existing wine package when installing Lutris
head: 5f0a1fe1035d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An already-installed wine-staging is mistaken for wine, so installing missing Lutris packages asks pacman to replace the working staging provider with wine and aborts
leads.consequence: With wine-staging present and Lutris (or any companion) missing, `pacman -Q wine` succeeds because wine-staging provides wine. The new condition therefore chooses wine, not wine-staging. `omarchy-pkg-missing` triggers `pacman -S --noconfirm --needed ... wine ...`; sync target selection picks literal wine, `--needed` compares actual local package names, and pacman's conflict-removal question defaults to no. Transaction fails, `omarchy-pkg-add` exits 1 and installer `set -e` prevents GPU setup, shebang fix and Lutris launch. On rerun the same choice and failure repeat. An installed third-party provider of wine is a similar risk if wine-staging is not installed; only wine-staging was verified from Arch's package recipe. Prefer omitting any explicit wine target if an installed package already satisfies wine, and add staging only if no provider exists (or resolve the provider's actual name).
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroboration; published as finding 1

leads.summary: Lutris removal deletes an existing wine user's prefix without removing (or distinguishing) the wine package
leads.consequence: The PR newly enables installation on a machine where wine and its existing ~/.wine prefix predate Lutris. The shipped Remove > Gaming > Lutris action then only supplies wine-staging to omarchy-pkg-drop; its exact-name installed list skips wine, but the remover unconditionally rm -rf's ~/.wine and wine caches anyway. Explicitly installed wine is left installed yet the user's unrelated existing prefix and its contents are destroyed, and the success message claims Wine was removed. The deleted prefix cannot be restored by reinstalling Lutris. Preserve pre-existing prefixes, or track package/prefix ownership and make destructive removal opt-in.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator read of remover lines 8-18 and in Opus final (Q3); published as pre-existing note with qualifiers from draft check D2-D4

leads.summary: Open PR #11364 already fixes #11301 in the same installer block; merging both requires resolving a real textual conflict and incompatible source-text tests
leads.consequence: #11364 independently changes the same removed install line and adds test/shell.d/lutris-wine-conflict-test.sh. This head and its head 1964c3b34b60a58c1ae7a4dabd82a6e4ebcedf90 are diverged, not stacked. Three-way git merge-file of both installer versions against their unchanged common base exits 1 and leaves conflict markers at merge-11364-lutris:9-24; no merged test can run until a maintainer chooses a guard. If one keeps only this PR's guard, #11364's test expects the absent literal `pacman -Qq wine`; if one keeps only #11364's guard, this PR's test expects absent `if omarchy-pkg-present wine`. Coordinate/consolidate the two fixes and replace both textual assertions with behavioral cases. GitHub's #11364 `mergeable: MERGEABLE` is against the current base tip, not the pairwise merge.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4); published as Overlap

leads.summary: The new regression test still passes when a later assignment forces the old, conflicting wine-staging target
leads.consequence: The test never runs the installer or probes the wine-detection result, only searches for three substrings. A plausible mutant keeps the conditional and all three rg matches but inserts `wine_pkg=wine-staging` just before pkg-add, reverting behavior for installed wine; the head test returned success against that mutant under LC_ALL=C. It also passes on the provider-conflict implementation in this head (H1). A runtime fixture should stub pacman and the install helpers, execute the real installer for installed wine, installed wine-staging and no provider, and assert the requested package targets and whether downstream steps run. The copied head test did fail against the unchanged current base tip, so this is a fidelity gap, not a missing registration.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); published as Test note

limits: No real pacman transaction or host package database was touched. H1 uses Arch shipped pacman/libalpm at packaging patch-level 54d9411 and Arch PKGBUILDs, not a simulated native package transaction; the text-only regression test and mutant were run within review.py.

flags.claim: The code also does not "use the installed wine provider" as the PR description says: it always asks for `wine`.
flags.why: 'always' is false as written: with no wine provider installed the head installer asks for wine-staging. It asks for the package named `wine` whenever anything that provides `wine` is installed. My handback used the same loose wording ('It always asks for literal wine'); final-report.md summary item 3 has the precise form.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed ('whenever anything that provides wine is installed, it asks for the package named wine')

flags.claim: `bin/omarchy-remove-gaming-lutris` removes `wine-staging` by exact name, so a user's own `wine` package stays installed
flags.why: Holds only if `wine` was explicitly installed (or is still required by another package). omarchy-pkg-drop runs `pacman -Rns`; single -s sets ALPM_TRANS_FLAG_RECURSE (not RECURSEALL), and _alpm_select_depends then also removes dependencies with reason=depend that nothing else needs. A `wine` pulled in as a dependency (for example by wine-mono or winetricks) would be removed together with wine-mono/wine-gecko/winetricks. Derived from source, not run. My own report (answer 3) and handback made the same unqualified claim.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed ('an explicitly installed wine stays installed')

flags.claim: Users who keep their own `wine` can reach the installer only with this PR.
flags.why: They can run the installer at base too; it fails there (base/wine exit 1). What changes is that the Omarchy install can now complete. Separately, the menu's Remove row only needs `omarchy-pkg-present lutris` (menu.jsonc:328), so a user with their own wine who installed Lutris some other way could already reach the remover at base.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed ('Before this PR the installer failed for users with their own wine; with it they can install Lutris and later remove it')

flags.claim: If they later remove Lutris from the menu, a Wine prefix they had before Lutris is deleted.
flags.why: The remover deletes only the default prefix path `$HOME/.wine` (plus caches). Prefixes at other paths are untouched. It also reaches rm -rf only after omarchy-pkg-drop succeeds (set -e). Not run.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed (default prefix ~/.wine only, after package removal succeeds)

flags.claim: `omarchy-remove-gaming-lutris` removes `wine-staging`, so this affects machines where it was installed some other way.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. My report said '(by hand, or when Lutris was removed without the Omarchy remover)'. A machine where this installer put wine-staging and Lutris was later removed with plain pacman is also affected, and that is not 'installed some other way'. My handback dropped the same parenthetical.
flags.disposition: real error; restored qualifier (by hand, or Lutris removed without the Omarchy remover)

flags.claim: **Optional test improvement:** ... It fails the working alternative above.
flags.why: Internal inconsistency rather than a false fact. If the Suggested change is adopted, the current test fails (alt-skip exit 1), so the test has to change with it; 'Optional' is only true if the PR keeps its current detection. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The change fixes the case from #11301. With `wine` installed (alone, or with `wine-mono` and `wine-gecko` as in the issue), the head installer asks for `wine`, and the pacman transaction succeeds, where the base installer aborts with the reported `wine-staging` / `wine` conflict. The main problem is the reverse case: an installed `wine-staging` now makes the installer fail.

### An installed `wine-staging` is detected as `wine`

`omarchy-pkg-present wine` runs `pacman -Q wine`. When no package is named `wine`, pacman falls back to matching provides (`src/pacman/query.c:481-483`, pacman v7.1.0), and `wine-staging` declares `provides=wine`. So the check succeeds for `wine-staging` too, and the installer then asks for the package literally named `wine`:

```text
installed: wine-staging (provides wine, conflicts wine)
  omarchy-pkg-present wine        -> pacman -Q wine prints "wine-staging 11.18-1", exit 0
  wine_pkg=wine
  pacman -S --noconfirm --needed lutris umu-launcher wine ...
    --needed skips only an installed package with the same name, so wine is a new target
    :: wine-11.18-1 and wine-staging-11.18-1 are in conflict. Remove wine-staging? [y/N]
    error: unresolvable package conflicts detected
  installer exits 1, nothing installed
```

The base installer succeeds in the same state (`wine-staging-11.18-1 is up to date -- skipping`).

**Impact:** The Lutris menu entry can only be selected while Lutris is not installed (`default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc:260`), so every menu install on a machine that already has `wine-staging` now fails. `omarchy-remove-gaming-lutris` removes `wine-staging`, so this affects machines where it was installed some other way (by hand, or when Lutris was later removed without the Omarchy remover). How common that is was not measured. Re-running the installer on a machine where everything is already installed is unaffected, because no transaction runs.

The code also does not "use the installed wine provider" as the PR description says: whenever anything that provides `wine` is installed, it asks for the package named `wine`. AUR providers such as `wine-git` and `wine-tkg-staging-wow64-bin` still fail the same way on both base and head.

| Installed before running the installer | base | head | alternative below |
|---|---|---|---|
| no wine | OK | OK | OK |
| `wine` | fails | OK | OK |
| `wine` + `wine-mono` + `wine-gecko` (#11301) | fails | OK | OK |
| `wine-staging` | OK | **fails** | OK |
| AUR `wine-git` | fails | fails | OK |
| AUR `wine-tkg-staging-wow64-bin` | fails | fails | OK |

**Suggested change:** Request no wine package when something already provides `wine`, and add `wine-staging` only when nothing does. `wine-mono`, `wine-gecko` and `winetricks` depend on `wine`, which the installed provider satisfies. This variant succeeded in all 8 modelled states in the isolated runs (the 6 above, plus the full package set already installed alongside `wine` or `wine-staging`):

```bash
packages=(lutris umu-launcher wine-mono wine-gecko winetricks python-protobuf)
if omarchy-pkg-missing wine; then
  packages+=(wine-staging)
fi
omarchy-pkg-add "${packages[@]}"
```

Limit (from package metadata, not run): AUR `wine-cachyos` also provides and conflicts with `wine-mono` and `wine-gecko`, so this variant would still conflict there.

**Overlap:** Open PR #11364 (opened 2026-09-11) also closes #11301 and keeps `wine-staging` when it is installed. In the same runs it succeeded in every state except the two AUR providers. The two PRs change the same lines of `bin/omarchy-install-gaming-lutris` and conflict in a merge, so landing one means reworking or closing the other.

**Test:** `test/shell.d/lutris-install-test.sh` only greps the installer source. It still passes when the detection checks `wine-staging` instead of `wine`, when the `wine_pkg=wine` assignment is removed (which brings back the #11301 failure), and when both wine packages are requested. It fails the working alternative above, so adopting that change also means changing the test. A runtime test like `test/shell.d/t3code-install-test.sh` (stubbed commands, real installer, assertions on the arguments passed to `omarchy-pkg-add`) would check the behavior, as `docs/testing.md` recommends. To catch the `wine-staging` case, the `pacman -Q` stub needs to answer `wine` when `wine-staging` is installed, not only on exact names.

**Related, pre-existing:** Before this PR the installer failed for users with their own `wine`; with it they can install Lutris and later remove it. `bin/omarchy-remove-gaming-lutris` (unchanged by this PR) drops `wine-staging` by exact name, so an explicitly installed `wine` stays installed. After the package removal succeeds, it still runs `rm -rf "$HOME/.wine"` (lines 10-18), which deletes the default Wine prefix even if it existed before Lutris.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the installer, the `omarchy-pkg-*` helpers, the remover, the menu entry and the new test at head `5f0a1fe1`, the merge base and the quattro tip `fd961e53`, plus pacman v7.1.0 source. Isolated runs used the real pacman 7.1.0 binary under fakeroot, with its root, database and cache in a throwaway directory, and synthetic packages carrying the real Arch and AUR depends/provides/conflicts entries for the wine packages (other dependencies left out, no files installed). `sudo`, `omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32`, `setsid` and `lutris` were stubbed. The states in the table were run for base, head, #11364 and the alternative. The new test was run against the head, base and the variants described. Real package installation, GPU driver selection and launching Lutris were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
